title: Automation state comes from its owners: the Tool base holds and exports what every tool shares; ui-state loses its per-scene branches (no reflection, no annotations)
description:
ui-state (automation/endpoints/ui/State.java, 640 lines) is a chain of `instanceof` branches on scene and tool types that copy hand-picked public fields (about 25 RingTool preview fields at 346-376). Every UI or tool change edits this file, and agents pipe the whole dump through python3 -c to pick fields (624 ui-state calls this week; top fields: ringTool 263, lastRow 73, mesh 70, error 68, confirmedRings 62, draft 61, previewValid 53, activeTool 39).

User direction 2026-10-21: no runtime reflection and no annotations. What every tool has in common is held and exported in ONE place, the Tool base, not re-created per tool. Today Tool is an interface (displayName, desc, info, addControls, escape, hover/click hooks) and the shared state is duplicated: `lastRow` on RingTool, ConnectionTool, RingRegionTool and RegionLayer; `lastError` on RingRegionTool; an EditHistory on RingTool and RoutePlanningTool. 8 classes implement Tool.

Design:
1. The Tool base holds the shared state once: the last result row, the last error, the edit history (EditHistory, or none), the current mode with its options, plus what it already declares (name, description, controls). The duplicated fields go. Tool stays named Tool (making it an abstract class is allowed; renaming is not).
2. The Tool base writes its own automation state in one method from that shared state; a tool adds only its own working state (RingTool: draft, preview, hover, confirmed rings) by overriding one hook, never by restating the shared fields.
3. Scenes contribute in the same way (the scene's datasets from ENG-37's Scene.dataset as summaries: fingerprints, counts, centroids, never raw arrays), and the pane boxes (MenuScrollBox) export their own text, rectangles and scroll.
4. State.java keeps only the common header (window, framebuffer, frames, focus, scene id) and asks the active scene, its tools and its panes for their parts. Existing top-level keys (mesh, trade, irregularGrid, ringTool/tool, textElements, menuItems, controls) stay, so the CLI and tests keep working.
definition-of-done:
1. State.java has no instanceof on a scene or tool type.
2. The last result row, last error, edit history heads and mode exist once, on the Tool base; no tool declares its own lastRow/lastError/history field.
3. A tool's automation state is written by the base from the shared state plus one per-tool hook for its own working state; nothing shared is restated per tool.
4. Every existing ui-state key keeps its name and value: a before/after recording of ui-state in ixdar-canvas, mesh-viewer, ring-tool (each tool active), trade and irregular-grid matches except listed, intended additions.
5. No runtime reflection and no new annotations.
6. mvn test and test_cli pass; launch entries and screenshots.

7. User rulings 2026-10-21 after the first pass:
   - Only ixdar.automation builds JSON. Tools, scenes, pane boxes, HyperString, ControlHint and ErrorToasts hold plain typed state and know nothing of JsonValue or export; automationState/addAutomationState and every JSON writer outside the automation package go.
   - Tool is a NON-generic abstract class holding the shared state (last row, last error, mode and options, name, description, controls), with overridable accessors a tool narrows by covariant return: history() (EditHistory<?>, null for no undo; RingTool returns EditHistory<RingToolState>), draft(), preview() and items(). Draft, Preview and Item are small common types (draft: points, valid; preview: hit point, valid, millis, detail text; item: label, location, fingerprint, saved/deleted); rings and routes implement them, and the exporter writes them the same way for every tool. No per-tool JSON hook, no per-tool re-listing of fields; diagnostics that fit none of these become preview detail text or are dropped (list them).
   - Scene data is exported per data type (PointSetPath, ModelCollection, RegionLayer, the mesh) through Scene.dataset(Subsystem), not per scene.
   - The rg leftovers go here: ui-state's "ring" waypoint block and RingScene's ringWaypointsXyz, ringWaypointCount, ring, closeRing, showRing, RING_SEED_LABEL, RING_TIGHTENED_LABEL (CRAW-74 and ENG-37 are on master).

8. User rulings 2026-10-22 (third pass):
   - Scene.panes() returns List<MenuScrollBox>, not List<Object>; the exporter writes every box the same way, labelled by its view id. The main menu's item labels become rows of a MenuScrollBox (buttons keep drawing as now), so menuItems/menuScroll derive from it; sceneMenuVisible is read from the boxes. No instanceof on pane types, and none on the trade grid type (the GRID dataset carries it).
   - Draft and Item share label, location, fingerprint, size (edge/segment count), length and a detail text; the base gains hovered() (the Item under the cursor) and the draft carries the Item it was reopened from. This restores hoveredRing, reopenedRing and the draft's and rings' edgeCount/length/fingerprint.
   - ConnectionTool fills draft (its two picks), preview (path and neck loop) and items; RingRegionTool fills items with the regions and their hide/isolate state. Confirmed rings come from the scene's shared ring set (RINGS dataset), not per tool, so a ring never appears under two tools.
   - The MESH dataset returns the shown GeometryBundle (slots, edge marks, repair report); shading comes from a common scene accessor and city pixels from the camera's point-to-pixel projection; State.java casts no scene type.
   - DoD 2 is amended: tools keep a typed history field behind the covariant history() override; no shared state is restated per tool.
testing-plan:
1. Record ui-state before any change in each scene with each tool active; compare after.
2. mvn test; uv run python -m unittest ixdar_automation_cli.test_cli.

changes-made: Tool is an abstract class Tool<S>: lastRow, lastError, history (EditHistory<S>, null without undo), modes/mode live there once; automationState() writes name, displayName, description, lastRow, error, undo heads, mode/modes and controls, then the one hook addAutomationState adds the tool's own state (RingTool: preview, draft, confirmed and drawn rings; RoutePlanningTool: route state, picks, route). The duplicated lastRow/lastError/history fields on RingTool, ConnectionTool, RingRegionTool and RoutePlanningTool and RingTool.newDraftMode/RoutePlanningTool.currentMode are gone (RegionLayer's layer summary is renamed summary). Scenes write their part through Scene.addAutomationState (mesh, trade, irregularGrid, collection, knotEditor, ringTool + errorToasts, menuItems/menuScroll) and their panes through Scene.addTextElements; MenuScrollBox, MenuScrollBar, HyperString, ControlHint and ErrorToasts export themselves. Exports are platform-neutral JsonValue trees (writer methods added; numbers keep int/float precision), converted to Gson only in State by GsonJsonTree.toGson. State.java 640 -> 167 lines; its only instanceof is the ring waypoint block, left verbatim for ENG-37. New top-level key tool (the active tool); ringTool gains name/displayName/description/mode/modes/controls. Before/after ui-state in 16 recordings (ixdar menu, trade picker/route/grow, irregular-grid, mesh-viewer +graph, ring-tool orbit/ring tool idle/draft/confirmed/crease, region and connection tools): no existing key changed. New test RouteToolAutomationStateTest; mvn test 570/0, test_cli 104/0.

Synced onto master eea66998 (ENG-37, CRAW-74, MESH-61); one conflict in ListCommand resolved (view.tools as Tool<?>). After the sync: mvn test 580/0, test_cli 104/0; re-recorded ui-state differs from the pre-change baseline only in mesh.slots (MESH-61's attribute layers on master) and the random game's city count. The ring waypoint block in State.java is still present on master and kept verbatim.

Second pass (user rulings, DoD 7): Tool is a plain abstract class (no generics) with lastRow, lastError, modes/mode and the accessors history() (EditHistory<?>, RingTool and RoutePlanningTool narrow it and keep their typed history field), draft(), preview(), items() returning the new common types Draft (points, valid), Preview (hitPoint, valid, millis, detail) and Item (label, location, fingerprint, saved, deleted). RingTool: draft = all anchors, valid when its trace marks edges; preview detail carries anchors, girdle edges, length, tolerance, deviation, geodesics, anchor cap, skeleton axis; items = confirmed rings. RoutePlanningTool: draft = picked cities, valid in PREVIEW; preview = hovered city with state and picks as detail; items = route segments. Every JSON writer outside ixdar.automation is gone (JsonValue/GsonJsonTree back to master); State.java writes the tool shape once for every tool, each dataset by its type through Scene.dataset (new Subsystem MESH, GRID, TRADE beside KNOT, MODEL, RINGS) and panes from Scene.panes(). rg leftovers deleted: ui-state ring block, RingScene ringWaypointsXyz/ringWaypointCount/ring/closeRing/showRing/RING_SEED_LABEL/RING_TIGHTENED_LABEL. ui-state before/after: all keys outside ringTool keep values except trade.routeState/selectedCityA/selectedCityB (now tool.preview.detail); ringTool reshaped to the common shape with values checked equal. mvn test 580/0, test_cli 104/0.

Third pass (DoD 8), uncommitted on 606ba97d: Item (label, location, fingerprint, size, length, detail, saved, deleted) with Draft extending it (points, pointLabels, valid, selectedPoint, hoveredPoint, reopened); Tool gains hovered(). RingTool fills draft (authored then supporting anchors, reopened ring), preview and hovered via ringItem(); confirmed rings come from RegionLayer.rings() (RINGS dataset, top-level rings) and no tool lists them. ConnectionTool fills draft (picks), preview (path/neck summary) and items (path, neck); RingRegionTool items are the regions with hidden/selected state in detail; RoutePlanningTool's draft is the operation labelled by its state with city-labelled points, hovered is the city under the cursor. Scene.panes() is List<MenuScrollBox>; the main menu's labels are rows of MenuBox.itemBox (sharing ITEM_COLUMN_SCROLL_BAR, rows placed on the buttons), which menuItems/menuScroll and sceneMenuVisible read. MESH dataset is the shown GeometryBundle (boundary/degenerate counts moved to MeshTopology defaults), shading via Scene.shaderModeName()/texturedDraw(), TRADE is the CityNetwork with pixels from scene.mouse.camera, GRID carries the trade map's irregular grid. State.java casts no scene type and has no instanceof on scene, tool, pane or grid types. ui-state vs original master: trade, menuItems, irregularGrid, collection unchanged; mesh only mesh.slots (MESH-61); textElements reshaped; ringTool reshaped (values checked). mvn test 592/0, test_cli 104/0.
review-summary: The Tool base and the scenes' datasets and panes now share Draft, Item and scroll-box shapes the ui-state route writes the same way for every tool, dataset and pane. Tools and scenes build no JSON, and the route no longer branches on scene, tool or pane types.
